lines.trans: They're books wrapped in plastic so you can't see inside.
They're a new kind of book that hides the contents to get people to buy them.
Whoever thought of this is sharp, aren't they?
About how many of these sell per month?
Apparently they sell over a million copies a month.
Calling me by my bare name all of a sudden, huh?
Well, that's Showtime for you. There's no turning back now.

meanings.note: Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Attaches to quantities or interrogatives (どのぐらい, 何本ぐらい) to indicate approximation.

examples.text: 一日何本ぐらい売れる？
examples.trans: About how many sell in a day?

examples.text: 十分ぐらい待ちました。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Interrogative prenoun adjectival; どのぐらい means 'about how much/many'.

examples.text: どのぐらいかかりますか。
examples.trans: About how long does it take?

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Evidential auxiliary adjective expressing hearsay or inference.

examples.text: 百万冊以上売れてるらしい。
examples.trans: Apparently it sells over a million copies.

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Muranishi's energetic younger partner in Sapporo.

examples.text: トシが外で待っています。
トシと一緒に来ました。

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'vinyl', used broadly for thin plastic film/bags.

examples.text: ビニールに包まれた本。

examples.trans: Put it in a plastic bag.

meanings.note: Refers to what is inside a package, book, or container.

examples.trans: A book whose contents you can't see.
Check the contents of the box.

meanings.note: Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb meaning to purchase merchandise for resale.

examples.text: これを仕入れることはできるか？
新しい商品を仕入れる。

meanings.note: Follows a number or quantity to indicate a lower bound (inclusive).

examples.text: 百万冊以上売れている。
examples.trans: Over a million copies are selling.
I waited more than ten minutes.

meanings.note: Polite volitional 会いましょう in また会いましょう means 'let us meet again'.

examples.trans: I meet a friend at the station.

examples.text: また来週会いましょう。

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.en: be sharp-minded; cut well; run out
meanings.note: Ichidan verb; in 頭が切れる, means 'be sharp/clever'.
Godan transitive verb; passive 包まれる means 'be wrapped in'.

examples.text: ビニールに包まれた本。
プレゼントを紙で包む。

meanings.en: addressing someone by bare name without honorifics
meanings.note: Dropping titles like さん or ちゃん, signaling intimacy or authority.

examples.trans: Calling me by my bare name all of a sudden, huh?

examples.text: 先輩を呼び捨てにしてはいけない。
examples.trans: You mustn't call a senior by their bare name.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb describing goods selling on the market without naming a seller.

examples.text: この絵本はよく売れます。
新しい本がたくさん売れました。
examples.trans: Many copies of the new book sold.

meanings.note: Often used with できる/できない (後戻りできない, 'cannot turn back').

examples.text: もう後戻りできないぞ。
今さら後戻りはしない。

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 急 (sudden).

examples.trans: Calling me by my bare name all of a sudden, huh?

meanings.note: Modifies nouns directly, as in 新しい店 ('new store') and 新しい仕事 ('new job').

examples.text: 新しい仕事が始まりました。
新しい靴を買いました。

meanings.note: Read つき when meaning 'month' or 'moon'; read げつ in month names.

examples.text: 月三千円のサービスです。
今月は仕事が多いです。
examples.trans: There is a lot of work this month.

meanings.note: Everyday word for books and bound publications.

examples.trans: I buy a book at the bookstore.

meanings.note: Number 百万 + counter 冊 (for bound volumes).

examples.text: 月に百万冊以上売れてるらしい。
examples.trans: Apparently they sell over a million copies a month.
A massive hit of one million copies.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: もう少しよく考えてみます。
examples.trans: I'll think about it a little more carefully.
I see that to be seen.

meanings.note: 買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.

meanings.note: Negative て-form 隠さなくて means 'without hiding / not hiding'.
In 頭が切れる, means 'sharp-minded / clever'.
